pages.text: Normally a bow's two limbs must be the same wood. Lay $(l)two different woods$() in the Fletching Table instead and you laminate a $(l)Composite Bow$(): one limb of each, and the stats of both.$(br2)Its tooltip names both woods.

pages.title: How It Blends
pages.text: $(li)$(l)Draw time$(): the average of the two$(li)$(l)Damage$(): the average of the two$(li)$(l)Traits$(): you keep $(o)every$() trait either wood has$(li)$(l)Effects$(): both woods' effects apply$(br2)So the numbers meet in the middle, but the perks stack.

pages.title: Worth Knowing
pages.text: That makes pairings the interesting part. $(l)Dark Oak$() and $(l)Birch$() land between a slow hammer and a fast flicker. $(l)Crimson$() and $(l)Warped$() gives you Ignited $(o)and$() No Gravity on one bow.$(br2)A composite crossbow works the same way, built from a composite bow at the bench.

pages.title: Turning It On
pages.text: Composites are $(o)off$() by default. Stacking traits is strong, so a server opts in deliberately.$(br2)Set $(l)composite_bows$() to true under $(l)crafting$() in the server config. While it is off, mismatched limbs simply will not assemble.
